dispatch: Two externally supplied aligned instruction/PC lanes accept RV32I ALU/LUI/AUIPC plus all six conditional branches, JAL and legal JALR. A CFI ends the accepted prefix: lane-zero CFI selects only lane zero, even when an unsupported tail is offered. An unsupported or misaligned-PC instruction within the selected prefix stalls that whole prefix. All selected ROB/IQ/physical/checkpoint resources are reserved from pre-cycle state. CFIs are eligible only on port zero; integers on either port. This profile uses synthetic instruction supply and pins explicit frontend-fault inputs to zero; the separate frontend fault profile checks that input path.
execution: Port zero uses control_flow_pipeline for integers and control flow; port one reuses alu_pipeline. Each holds one ROB identity and full computed event. Branch conditions use the consumed PRF values, including accepted-write bypass. JAL/JALR produce PC+4 links; JALR clears target bit zero before the 4-byte alignment check. Misaligned taken targets produce a fault without link write. execution_ready_i qualifies issue independently per port.
completion: completion_enable_i grants the two fixed producer slots independently of resolution. Only completion_accept_o releases the producer. An accepted resolution with denied completion retains the result/link and cannot repeat resolution or redirect. Non-CFIs retain the previous consume/refill behavior. x0 and faults complete without a PRF write. Only accepted nonzero writes drive PRF payload, readiness and wakeup. LSU/multi-producer arbitration is not implemented.
recovery: Accepted misprediction preserves the branch and older work, suppresses allocation/issue/retirement that cycle, restores the branch checkpoint and kills younger ROB/IQ entries. Port zero holds the sole current resolver; only a younger port-one held result needs selective cancellation in this topology. Its age is compared modulo 32 against the pre-cycle ROB head, independently of its completion grant. An older port-one result survives and may complete/write in the recovery cycle. Already completed younger results and already resolved younger branches are reclaimed by existing backend recovery. External reset/full-window flush suppresses resolution/completion and clears both producers with speculative backend state. Flush preserves committed registers, event order and generation-use history.
events: Events capture instruction, before/after PC, architectural source addresses and consumed values, and computed destination result. Unused sources use p0. Faults suppress rd address/value/mask, not just writeback. M-mode and zero memory/CSR effects apply to this execution profile; ROB supplies retirement order. Nonzero initial GPR payloads remain unspecified, so tests initialize every register they read.
lint: Baseline .vlt waivers cover intentionally open boundary outputs, unused generated platform constants and unused decoded fields in execute_single. No width or combinational-loop warning is waived. Assertion-disabled mutation builds additionally permit signals/constants made unused by injected faults.
scope: Connected two-wide integer plus branch/jump execution with synthetic instruction/prediction supply, real PRF operands, actual resolution, held completion, selective port-one cancellation and ordered normal retirement. Not a complete processor: no fetch, predictor/history repair, LSU, multi-event oldest-recovery arbiter, CSR/trap head controller, architectural-suite promotion of this top, integrated formal proof or physical timing closure. Existing integer_backend remains its separate accepted subset. FPGA is excluded; clock/architecture review after full verification and LibreLane GDSII remain future gates. Explicit frontend fault injection is available; its acceptance evidence is the separate frontend_faults profile.
prediction: The caller supplies predicted_taken_i and predicted_pc_i for each accepted CFI. Both are saved under its live ROB slot and read on actual issue. The IQ still carries the existing 64-bit instruction/PC payload; prediction metadata is a sidecar owned by this top. New CFI allocation overwrites the sidecar before issue, including after slot or generation reuse. No predictor, speculative GHR/RAS or training is implemented.
resolution: Only the actually launched port-zero non-faulting CFI offers resolution. Its identity, actual taken outcome, next PC and misprediction flag stay held until resolve_accept_o. Misprediction means either direction or next-PC mismatch, including direction-only mismatch with an equal next PC. resolve_grant_i is external permission from the future oldest-event arbiter and must also reserve redirect-consumer capacity for a misprediction. resolve_accept_o atomically resolves ROB/checkpoint state; redirect_o is its misprediction pulse and resolve_pc_o the accepted target. The producer remembers acceptance exactly once. It offers completion starting in the following cycle, never before or in the resolution cycle.
faults: Faulting CFIs complete with trap_cause=instruction-address-misaligned, trap_value=the bad target after JALR bit-zero clearing, retired=0, and all destination fields zero. They do not resolve or redirect speculatively; their checkpoints remain until full flush. fault_pending_o and fault_event_o expose the held ROB-head fault candidate. trap_ready is tied low: no CSR trap-entry controller, architectural trap event finalization, mtvec redirect or accepted trap-order transition is implemented. fault_event.pc_after remains the computed target and CSR effects are zero; this candidate must not be published as a finalized architectural trap event. The test driver examines the stable candidate and explicitly flushes to continue; that flush does not claim architectural trap service.
drain: drained_i is caller-coordinated global quiescence: no ROB/IQ work, held producer (including unresolved CFI), offered instructions/completions/resolution, or external holders. Exhausted 8-bit generations never silently wrap. The top checks producer_busy_o as well as the existing backend guards. No automatic drain coordinator is added.
frontend_fault_injection: frontend_fault_i overrides decoding on selected lanes with a resultless, source-free, destination-free, non-CFI token. A lane-zero fault ends the accepted prefix. Cause/value/original instruction/PC are captured at allocation under the ROB slot, and fault membership is overwritten on every allocation. Completion replaces the internal neutral scheduling token with a raw trap candidate (pc_after=pc_before, retired=0, no register/memory/CSR effects). Both producer ports can hold faults. Existing recovery and generation checks govern acceptance. The original execution test pins these inputs to zero; frontend_faults-check exercises insertion. Trap service is still absent.
